item.title: Montgomery Multiplication: Theory Vs Practice
item.description: In a recent blog post, Yuval Domb describes a subtle, but remarkably clever optimisation that allows us to compute the Montgomery product of two integers modulo a $n$-limb1 integer $p$, using $2n^2 + 1$ multiplication operations. Previously, the best known algorithm2 for Montgomery multiplication was known to use $2n^2 + n$ multiplication operations. Despite this theoretical promise of fewer multiplications, we did not see physical speedups in runtime when testing the new algorithm empirically against the old algorithms. This post is a deep dive into why this could be, and potentially what can be done about it.
